question.text: The inactivation rate of a viral preparation is proportional to the amount of virus. In the first minute after preparation, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo>%</mo></math> of the virus is inactivated. The rate constant for viral inactivation is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>min</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>.</mo></math> (Nearest integer) [Use : <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>ln</mi><mn>10</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>303</mn><mo>;</mo><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>10</mn></msub><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>477</mn></math> property of logarithm<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced close="]" open=""><mrow><mo>:</mo><mi>log</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>y</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>y</mi><mi>log</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfenced></math>

solution.text:
As the unit of rate constant is min-1 so it must be a first order reaction
k×t=2.303logA0/At
in 1 min 10% is inactivated so taking
A0=100   At=90 in 1 min
So k×1=2.303×log10090

=2.303×(log10-2log3)
=2.303×(1-2×0.477)
=0.10593

=105.93×10-3
Answer is 106
